samples.reason: ck-pi-zen-session 0.1.13 is a disclosed OpenCode Zen session/model configuration extension for the Pi coding agent. Original npm registry archive is byte-identical. Its API-key reads are provider configuration lookup; the network request sends that same provider key to https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/models. Results are parsed as model metadata, never executed. It writes Pi models/auth JSON and updates matching provider rows in the optional CC-Switch SQLite database. Its Python -c child is a locally constructed SQLite compatibility fallback, not a fetched payload. There are no install lifecycle hooks. This purposeful, transparent integration tips the verdict BENIGN despite deliberate client impersonation and session rotation to avoid free-tier failures.

reverse_engineering.index.ts: Pi extension initialization replaces fetch, registers the provider and zen command, and registers before_provider_headers/request, after_provider_response and before_agent_start callbacks. Only selected Zen models get event-hook payload transformations. The global fetch wrapper gates on a substring opencode.ai/zen/v1; it rewrites headers, injects or sorts tool schemas, normalizes reasoning parameters, and passes the request to the saved fetch. It schedules configuration refresh on 401/403. Those tool schemas are declarations, not embedded implementations of bash/read/write.
reverse_engineering.sync.ts: Provider API key comes from explicit user command, three provider-specific environment variables, or provider entries in the configured auth/models files. fetchZenModelCatalog performs GET /models with Bearer authentication and configured client User-Agent. It filters free models and updates configuration only after catalog resolution or a documented fallback. JSON writes preserve other provider entries. SQLite updates are limited by provider ID and app_type. Native SQLite uses bound parameters; fallback builds a Python sqlite3 script and calls execFileSync(python3, [-c, script], timeout=3000). The fallback interpolates local path/key values without escaping, which is an injection vulnerability rather than evidence of active exploitation.
reverse_engineering.session.ts: SHA-256 of cwd creates a stable project ID. Session/request IDs combine timestamp and a counter, encode six bytes as hex, and append 14 random Base62 characters. Session IDs invert timestamp bits for descending order; this is identifier encoding, not hidden executable code. IDs expire after 30 minutes; timestamp extraction resolves the truncated 36-bit cycle.
reverse_engineering.models-registry.ts: Static model descriptions and tool JSON schemas, plus model-capability inference and UI formatting. The endpoint constant is the real Zen API. No remote JavaScript loader, payload staging or concealed stage was found.
reverse_engineering.packaging: Eight regular archive members, source TypeScript entrypoint declared in pi.extensions, no installation hooks, MIT license and monorepo repository.directory declaration. The peer dependency is a host supplied API; index.ts imports its types only. No hidden binary or obfuscated executable layer was present in the archive or decoded facts.
reverse_engineering.limits: No deployment history or external-source labeling rationale was provided. Node is unavailable, so extension behavior was established by full source/control-flow and argument analysis, not a live extension run. Potential interceptor recursion on an expired persisted session and substring URL gating are implementation risks, not evidence of malicious intent. Package-registry identity and documentation alone did not determine the verdict.

external_label_disagreement: Both shell files are exact public BusyBox test sources and have only re-execution/echo test behavior; the external flag may be inherited collection context or an exec heuristic, but that origin is not supplied. The Zen extension intentionally impersonates an official client, rotates free-tier sessions, accesses provider keys, and runs a Python fallback; these can explain heuristic suspicion, yet no covert transfer, backdoor, unauthorized persistence or downloaded code execution is supported.
